subject: Post-demo: quantifying tail-latency & streaming resilience for private deployment
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@stratoshealth.com>, Leah Morrison <leah.m@stratoshealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Sep 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: quantifying tail-latency & streaming resilience for private deployment

Thanks again for your time on the demo today — great conversation. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so we can line up the network/ops validation with your infra team.

Key points from the call:
- Latency goals you mentioned: p50 ~25–35ms, p95 <150ms for 512-token responses; p99 requires more investigation (you flagged tail latency concerns).
- Streaming: client expects chunked, near-real-time token delivery for chat (must support partial tokens and mid-stream cancellations).
- Concurrency: target baseline ~200 concurrent streaming sessions, with burst tolerance up to ~400 for short spikes.
- Deployment: private deployment in your AWS account via VPC Peering or Transit Gateway (you said peering is preferred; we discussed VPN as fallback). Egress path will originate from your VPC to our inference subnets.

Immediate asks for the network/ops preflight so we can scope acceptance testing:
1) Share network topology PDF/diagram (public peering details redacted if necessary) — see attached template (request-template-network-info.xlsx).
2) Provide a sample traceroute/ICMP ping stats from your app subnet to the proposed peering endpoint (avg RTT, jitter, packet loss).
3) Confirm estimated sustained concurrency window: are spikes expected to last >5 minutes or <1 minute?
4) Any MTU/custom firewall/NAT devices that could fragment WebSocket frames or long-lived TCP connections?

Proposed technical validation plan (we'll run this jointly):
- Short smoke: connect, handshake, stream a 128-token response to validate chunking and keepalive behavior.
- Load step: synthetic ramp to 250 concurrent streaming sessions with 256-token messages for 2m sustained to measure p50/p95/p99 per-token latency and rebuffer events.
- Tail-latency focused run: smaller batch with synthetic cold cache/kv-warmup to reproduce any p99 outliers.

Next steps I propose this week:
- You share topology & ping results (item 1–2 above).
- Karthik and I run a 30-minute network preflight with your infra lead to validate peering and MTU. Proposed slots: Thu 09/22 10:00–10:30 PT or Fri 09/23 14:00–14:30 PT.

Attachments: redwood_demo_recording.mp4, request-template-network-info.xlsx

Thanks — happy to adjust the test plan once we have your topology.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
+a (555) 210-8810

Thanks Aisha — good summary. A few clarifications from our side before we schedule the preflight: 

- Tail / p99: our production SLO is p99 < 300ms for short messages; the team is most concerned about p99 with streaming because a small number of slow connections kills UX. If we hit p95 targets but see p99 spikes, what mitigation knobs do we have short of over-provisioning?

- Streaming chunking: are chunks fixed-size or adaptive? What is the default frame size and can we tune it per-connection? Our clients will likely use 1KB–8KB chunk sizes depending on platform.

- Keepalive & idle timeouts: what TCP/TLS idle timeouts does Redwood expect for long-lived streams? We have some intermediate NAT gateways that drop idle TCP after 90s — will that be a problem?

- Peering: we will be using AWS Transit Gateway between our VPCs and the Redwood peering subnets (we'll share topology). Security team also requested SOC2 checklist and a sample audit log for token access — do you have a redacted artifact we can share with compliance?

- Pricing: can you give a rough order-of-magnitude estimate for per-1M tokens for a private/dedicated deployment so we can model costs for our procurement?

Attaching network-topology-v1.pdf (contains private IPs redacted).

Rajiv

Hi Rajiv — thanks for the questions and for the topology file. I'm Marissa (solutions), copying Karthik (network lead) and Rohan (SRE) for the preflight work. Quick answers + a proposed checklist.

Tail/p99 mitigation options (short-term & long-term):
- Short-term: configure request-side timeouts and aggressive circuit breakers at the app layer; Redwood can be configured to drop very slow connections and return a graceful fallback payload. That avoids cascading slow streams.
- Medium-term: use a smaller model variant for low-latency tails (we can configure automatic fallback on latency thresholds).
- Long-term: prefix caching and KV warmup will reduce token-generation variability on repeated patterns.

Streaming chunking and tunables:
- Default: chunking is adaptive; we typically emit token batches in ~4–8KB frames for text models. Frames are configurable per-connection in the proxy layer.
- You can tune max frame size client-side; if you expect small mobile chunks (1KB), we'll accept them but recommend a clip-and-aggregate strategy to reduce small-packet overhead.

Keepalive / idle timeouts:
- Expected behavior: we use persistent TLS/TCP for streaming. Default keepalive probe interval: 30s; recommended idle timeout tolerance is >=120s.
- For NATs that tear connections at ~90s we recommend either lowering keepalive interval or enabling application-level ping (we can provide a lightweight ping sample).

Peering notes & compliance artifacts:
- We can provide a redacted SOC2 evidence pack and a sample audit log (redacted) for your security team; I'll attach a stub checklist now.

Proposed concrete preflight plan (30–45m):
1) Confirm IPs/subnets and peering method (Transit Gateway vs direct VPC Peering).
2) Run traceroute/ping to our peering endpoint; collect RTT distribution and packet loss.
3) Smoke stream: handshake + 128-token stream to validate chunking and keepalive.
4) Load step: synthetic ramp to 250 conc. sustained 2m with 256-token sequences to capture p50/p95/p99.
5) Tail run: 1–2 short runs with cold caches to surface p99 behaviors.

Attachments: net-preflight-checklist.md
Links: test script and dashboards (shared folder) - https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1q2-demo-assets

I'll prepare the SOC2 redacted pack and a sample audit log and share by EOD. Karthik — can you confirm whether the Transit Gateway setup will require any additional route advertisement or will standard TGW attachment suffice?

Thanks — happy to run the preflight in either slot Aisha proposed.

— Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
